recipes.title: Turmeric Ginger Chicken Curry
recipes.description: A comforting, anti-inflammatory curry that's easy to digest and provides protein and calories to help maintain weight during chemotherapy.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cubed
instructions: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, and coriander. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat with the spices. Cook for 5 minutes, until the chicken is lightly browned.
Pour in the chicken broth and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20-25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro. Enjoy over steamed basmati rice.
recipes.clinical_notes: This curry is rich in anti-inflammatory spices like turmeric and ginger, which can help manage nausea and taste changes. The coconut milk provides calories and healthy fats, while the chicken offers lean protein to support muscle maintenance. The soft texture and gentle flavors make it easy to digest during chemotherapy.
recipes.tips: For patients with a poor appetite, consider serving smaller portions more frequently. You can also blend the curry into a soup or sauce consistency if chewing is difficult.

recipes.title: Soothing Masala Khichdi
recipes.description: A comforting, easy-to-digest rice and lentil porridge that provides complex carbs, fiber, and protein to nourish patients during chemotherapy.
ingredients: 1/2 cup split yellow moong dal (or red lentils), rinsed
4 cups water or low-sodium vegetable broth
instructions: In a large pot, heat the ghee or oil over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cloves. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the rinsed rice and lentils. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in the water or broth and stir in the turmeric, coriander, and cumin.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice and lentils are very soft and porridge-like.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.
recipes.clinical_notes: Khichdi is a classic Indian comfort food that's easy on the digestive system, making it an excellent choice for chemotherapy patients dealing with nausea, mouth sores, and other GI side effects. The combination of rice and lentils provides complex carbs, fiber, and plant-based protein to help maintain weight and energy levels. The warming spices like turmeric and cumin also have anti-inflammatory properties.
recipes.tips: For patients with poor appetite, try serving smaller portions more frequently. You can also blend the khichdi into a smoother texture if chewing is difficult. Add extra broth or water to thin it out as needed.

recipes.title: Chickpea and Vegetable Curry
recipes.description: This flavorful and nourishing curry is packed with protein, fiber, and anti-inflammatory spices to support long-term health and cancer prevention. The soft texture is easy to digest.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (diced carrots, bell peppers, spinach)
instructions: In a large pot, sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger in a little oil until fragrant.
Add the spices and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in the vegetable broth and coconut milk, then add the chickpeas and vegetables.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the lemon juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over basmati rice or with naan bread.
recipes.clinical_notes: This curry is an excellent source of plant-based protein, fiber, and anti-inflammatory spices like turmeric. The soft texture is easy to digest, and the blend of vegetables provides a variety of nutrients to support long-term health and cancer prevention.
recipes.tips: For patients with a poor appetite, try serving smaller portions more frequently. If fatigue is an issue, prepare the curry in advance and reheat as needed.

recipes.title: Mango Lassi Smoothie
recipes.description: This creamy, refreshing lassi smoothie is packed with vitamins, minerals, and anti-inflammatory properties from the mango, yogurt, and spices. It's a great way to boost nutrition and hydration, especially for patients struggling with appetite or weight management.
instructions: Add all ingredients to a high-speed blender and blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour into glasses and enjoy immediately.
recipes.clinical_notes: This mango lassi smoothie provides a nutrient-dense, high-calorie option that can help address common challenges like nausea, fatigue, and weight loss. The yogurt and spices also have anti-inflammatory properties to support long-term health.
recipes.tips: For patients with a sensitive stomach, start with a smaller portion and gradually increase. The honey can be omitted if desired.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Baked Cod with Roasted Veggies
recipes.description: This flavorful baked cod dish is packed with Mediterranean-inspired ingredients that are gentle on the stomach and provide essential nutrients during chemotherapy.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large baking dish, arrange the cod fillets and scatter the diced bell peppers, zucchini, cherry tomatoes, and onion around the fish.
Drizzle the olive oil over the vegetables and fish, and sprinkle with the dried oregano, basil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Serve the baked cod and roasted vegetables warm.
recipes.clinical_notes: This recipe is high in protein and fiber, which can help maintain weight and support digestion during chemotherapy. The Mediterranean-style ingredients and baking method are gentle on the stomach and provide anti-inflammatory benefits.
recipes.tips: For patients with mouth sores, you can puree the cooked vegetables to create a softer texture. Adjust seasoning to personal taste preferences.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Vegetable and Lentil Soup
recipes.description: This nourishing and comforting Mediterranean-style vegetable and lentil soup is easy to digest, hydrating, and packed with essential nutrients to support patients during chemotherapy.
instructions: In a large pot, combine the rinsed lentils, diced onion, minced garlic, carrots, celery, and zucchini.
Add the diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, dried oregano, dried basil, and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are tender.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.
Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with chopped parsley, if desired.
recipes.clinical_notes: This Mediterranean-inspired vegetable and lentil soup is a great option for breast cancer patients during chemotherapy. The lentils provide plant-based protein, while the vegetables and broth offer hydration and essential nutrients. The soft texture is gentle on the stomach and easy to digest, making it suitable for patients experiencing side effects like nausea, mouth sores, and dry mouth.
recipes.tips: For patients with difficulty swallowing, you can blend the soup to a smoother, pureed consistency. Adjust seasoning to personal taste preferences.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Salmon and Vegetable Bake
recipes.description: This easy one-pan bake features omega-3 rich salmon, fiber-filled vegetables, and Mediterranean herbs and spices. It's a nutritious and comforting meal that can help support long-term health and cancer prevention.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Arrange the salmon fillets, tomatoes, onion, zucchini, and bell pepper on a large baking sheet.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with oregano, thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the salmon is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Serve immediately.
recipes.clinical_notes: This recipe is high in omega-3 fatty acids, antioxidants, and fiber, which can support long-term health and cancer prevention. The Mediterranean-style flavors and one-pan preparation make it an easy, nutritious meal for patients who may be experiencing fatigue or weight management challenges.
recipes.tips: For patients with a poor appetite, try serving smaller portions or pairing this with a simple side salad.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Quinoa Stuffed Eggplant
recipes.description: These Mediterranean-inspired stuffed eggplants are packed with fiber, protein, and anti-inflammatory ingredients to support long-term health and cancer prevention. The quinoa and vegetable filling provides a satisfying and nutrient-dense meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Scoop out the flesh from the eggplant halves, leaving a 1/4-inch border. Chop the eggplant flesh.
In a skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped eggplant, onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the cooked quinoa, tomatoes, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Spoon the quinoa mixture back into the eggplant shells.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the eggplant is tender.
Serve warm.
recipes.clinical_notes: This recipe is a great source of fiber, protein, and antioxidants from the quinoa, vegetables, and Mediterranean herbs and spices. The eggplant provides a low-calorie, nutrient-dense base that can help support healthy weight management and long-term cancer prevention.
recipes.tips: For patients with a poor appetite, try serving smaller portions or pairing this with a simple side salad.

advice.key_recommendation: Focus on maintaining weight, muscle mass, and adequate nutrition during chemotherapy.
advice.detailed_guidance: Chemotherapy can significantly impact appetite, taste, and the ability to eat. It's important to prioritize nutrient-dense foods that can help maintain weight and muscle mass, which are crucial for tolerating treatment and preparing for surgery.

Fruits and vegetables in a variety of colors

Lentil and vegetable stew with whole-grain bread
practical_tips: Eat small, frequent meals throughout the day
Keep nutrient-dense snacks on hand
Consider using a nutritional supplement if appetite is poor
advice.clinical_context: Maintaining adequate nutrition is crucial during chemotherapy to support the body's ability to tolerate treatment, prevent weight loss, and prepare for surgery.
